cast.subject: Fact — the concept space of fact in philosophical discourse: what is the case, what makes true, what is instituted, what one is thrown into, what is made

file.source: Husserl, Logical Investigations (Sachverhalt); Wittgenstein, Tractatus 2–2.01; Russell, The Philosophy of Logical Atomism (1918); Armstrong, A World of States of Affairs (1997); Durkheim, The Rules of Sociological Method (1895); Searle, The Construction of Social Reality (1995); Heidegger, Being and Time §29 (Faktizität); Sartre, Being and Nothingness; Fleck, Genesis and Development of a Scientific Fact (1935); Latour & Woolgar, Laboratory Life (1979)

counts-as.meaning: X counts as Y in context C (Searle): the first is taken as the second under a constitutive rule

constituted-by.meaning: the first is constituted by the second (collective representation, thought collective, constitution)

thrown-into.meaning: the first finds itself delivered over to the second (Geworfenheit)

independent-of.meaning: the first obtains independently of the second

cast.subject: Value — the concept space of value in philosophical discourse: the good in itself, the instrumental, the posited, the fitting, the valid

file.source: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics I.7; Moore, Principia Ethica (1903); Dewey, Theory of Valuation (1939); Marx, Capital I ch. 1 (use value); Nietzsche, On the Genealogy of Morals (Wertsetzung); Heidegger, 'Nietzsche's Word: God is Dead'; Brentano, The Origin of our Knowledge of Right and Wrong (1889); Scheler, Formalism in Ethics (1913); Scanlon, What We Owe to Each Other (1998); Weber, 'Science as a Vocation' (1919); Habermas, The Theory of Communicative Action (1981); Kant, Groundwork

for-the-sake-of.meaning: the first is chosen or valued for the sake of the second

posits.meaning: the first posits the second as a value (a valuation sets it)

merits.meaning: the first merits the second (a fitting attitude, a correct love)

binds.meaning: the first binds the second (an ought, a validity claim that obliges)

independent-of.meaning: the first holds independently of the second

cast.subject: Meaning — the concept space of meaning in philosophical discourse: sense, reference, use, difference, significance

file.source: Frege, 'On Sense and Reference' (1892); Husserl, Ideas I (noema); Russell, 'On Denoting' (1905); Wittgenstein, Philosophical Investigations §43; Austin, How to Do Things with Words (1962); Saussure, Course in General Linguistics (1916); Derrida, Of Grammatology (1967), 'Différance' (1968); Dilthey, The Formation of the Historical World; Heidegger, Being and Time §32; Gadamer, Truth and Method (1960)

determines.meaning: the first determines the second (sense determines reference; difference determines sense)

constituted-by.meaning: the first is constituted by the second (meaning constituted by use)

defers.meaning: the first defers the second (presence, reference, significance postponed in the play of differences)

projects.meaning: the first is that upon which the second is projected (significance as the Woraufhin of understanding)

independent-of.meaning: the first holds independently of the second

cast.subject: Action — the concept space of action in philosophical discourse: intention, reason, the deed, the communicative act, imputation

file.source: Anscombe, Intention (1957); Davidson, 'Actions, Reasons, and Causes' (1963); Arendt, The Human Condition (1958); Nietzsche, On the Genealogy of Morals I §13; Hegel, Philosophy of Right §§115–118; Austin, How to Do Things with Words (1962); Habermas, The Theory of Communicative Action (1981); Kant, Metaphysics of Morals 6:227 (Zurechnung); Ricoeur, Oneself as Another (1990)

rationalizes.meaning: the first rationalizes the second (a primary reason shows the action in a favourable light)

under-description.meaning: the first is what it is under the description the second gives

begins.meaning: the first begins the second (natality: action starts a new chain among others)

answers-for.meaning: the first answers for the second (ascription, responsibility)

independent-of.meaning: the first holds independently of the second
